jobs.description: Overview Physical Superintelligence is a startup with roots at Google, NVIDIA, Harvard, Meta, MIT, Oxford, Johns Hopkins, Cambridge, and the Perimeter Institute building AI systems to discover new physics at scale. We are seeking engineers to build platform infrastructure at the intersection of computational science, AI systems, and software engineering. Our mission is to discover and commercialize transformative physics breakthroughs at scale with artificial superintelligence, safely, verifiably, and for broad public benefit. The last century's golden age of physics gave us transistors, lasers, and nuclear energy. We believe artificial superintelligence will unlock the next one. We're creating the infrastructure to industrialize scientific discovery and usher in this new era. We have one product: new physics, at scale. Use this application if you are an engineer, no open engineering role fits your profile, and you want to be considered anyway. We hire excellent engineers when we find them, whether or not a matching role is open. Tell us how your background and ambitions intersect with our mission, and where you would have the most impact. Â Role and Responsibilities Our platform spans distributed systems, data infrastructure, agent systems and evaluation, HPC and scientific computing, developer platforms, product engineering, cloud infrastructure, and security. This application is for engineers who are strong across most of that list, or unusually deep in something important we did not list. The bar here is higher than any single posting. The standard is the same as every engineering role here: full ownership from spec to ship to on-call, and systems other people build on. Be specific about where you would have the most impact and what you would work on first. We review these applications on a rolling basis and respond only when we see a strong fit. What We're Looking For A track record of shipping substantive engineering work: systems that shipped and mattered, open source people depend on, infrastructure that outlived your tenure. We weight evidence over credentials. Depth in several of the areas above and the range to move between them, or singular depth in something important we did not list. You can walk us through a hard technical decision you made, what you traded away, and what you would do differently. A concrete reason to be here. If AI systems and physical science together is why you are applying, say so specifically. Nice to Have Background in any of our named areas: distributed systems, data infrastructure, agent systems and evals, HPC and scientific computing, developer platforms, product engineering, infrastructure, or security. Experience in research or scientific computing environments. Something we can read or run: a design doc, a paper, a repo, a postmortem. Â How We Work We hold a high technical bar and give people full ownership of their work, from spec to ship to on-call. We write contracts before logic, test against real systems instead of mocks, and favor simple designs that ship over clever ones that do not. Our development process is AI-native: we work with agentic coding tools daily, write specs that are legible to humans and agents alike, and lead with leverage. Â Location and Compensation This role is based in Boston. We will consider remote candidates on a case-by-case basis. We offer competitive compensation including salary, benefits, and meaningful early-stage equity. We evaluate on technical breadth, systems thinking, scientific curiosity, and shipping velocity. We are an equal opportunity employer and value diverse perspectives in building platforms for AI-driven discovery. Brand presence and consistent messaging are essential enablers of our success. As the Marketing Director (m/w/d) at Exolaunch, you will serve as a core strategic leader driving our global marketing, brand presence, and multi-channel social media accounts, while exercising hands-on ownership of our public image, press relations, and executive communications. We’re looking for a visionary marketing leader and creative storyteller with deep expertise in luxury branding, premium positioning, and high-impact copywriting. Protocol and integration architecture Evolve the schema that defines how every sensor, asset, and mission system talks to Hydris. Those issues live in the code they write, and you set the technical direction for the static analysis engine that finds them.</p> <p>Your work spans two complementary parts of a complete security analysis. On the engine side, you shape how the static analysis toolkit models a program: parsing source into intermediate representations, resolving symbols, building call graphs, and tracking tainted data across files and languages. You define the architecture and specifications the team builds against, and you delegate component specifications within them to engineers and to the AI agents that implement them. On the evaluation side, you build and apply tooling that tests, measures, and validates what the engine finds against benchmark applications with known vulnerabilities.</p> <p>What the engine can model and how we measure what it finds are parts of one picture. As a Staff engineer you hold that picture, shape the long-range technical goals of the team, and raise the bar for every engineer on it. We build the engine with AI agents that write and review code from written specifications, under human direction. We expect you to direct that work effectively and with good judgment, and to help the team do the same.</p> <h3><strong>What you do</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Act as the directly responsible individual (DRI) for the team's highest-scope initiatives from design through delivery, shipping large features with minimal guidance and shaping the long-range goals of the team</li> <li>Bring systems built by one engineer to team ownership through documentation, tests, and shared review</li> <li>Set the technical direction for the AI-assisted tooling that implements, reviews, and validates engine changes and findings, design the checks that decide whether an agent-written change or generated result is fit to merge, and measure detection quality against benchmark applications with known vulnerabilities, raising the bar for what counts as a trustworthy result. That includes static application security testing (SAST) rules mapped to CWE and OWASP, and the test fixtures that prove they work.&

jobs.title: Data Scientist (Credit) - Car Finance
jobs.description: We’re on a mission to make migration easy. We started building Marshmallow in 2017. Since then, we’ve grown from 3 to 700+ people, gained unicorn status, raised ~£140M over three funding rounds, turned profitable, insured millions of drivers and lent millions in car loans. But we’re only just getting started. Our goal is to become one of the largest financial services providers in the world. Over the next 10 years we’ll grow exponentially, not only by scaling our existing products, but also by building new ones. To achieve our goals we need incredibly ambitious, commercially driven people who never settle for ‘good enough’. Marshmallowers are hungry for autonomy and ownership, and would rather improve than coast. Everyone raises standards and has an impact, with a focus on collective success over self-interest. We’ve created an environment where curious, tenacious people win and grow together. If that sounds motivating, this could be the place for you. London (hybrid, 3 days in office) Car Finance at Marshmallow Marshmallow is opening up access to credit to migrants, bringing a brand new product to market which provides newcomers to the UK with fairly priced car finance for the first time. Our Car Finance team is building a new generation lending platform from the ground up, making it simple, transparent and accessible for people who need finance to get on the road. We work closely with dealers, brokers and customers to make sure that every application, decision and interaction is fast, fair and easy to understand. Because we’re a small, high-performing team, everyone has real ownership. We combine hands-on operations with a strong focus on automation and technology. We’re designing highly automated, AI-powered processes that let us move faster and smarter than traditional lenders. The Role We're hiring a Data Scientist to sit at the heart of how we lend: who we say yes to, at what price, and how we know it's working. Our customers are people that traditional lenders struggle to assess. Many are new to the UK, have thin or no credit files, and don't fit neatly into off-the-shelf bureau scores. That makes credit decisioning at Marshmallow a genuinely hard, genuinely interesting problem: we combine bureau data, Open Banking, insurance, application and behavioural data to build a view of risk that others can't, and we need to do it in a way that is fair, explainable and compliant. This role sits between a traditional credit analyst and a data scientist. You'll build and monitor scorecards, design and test credit strategies, dig into portfolio performance to find out what's really going on, and turn large, messy datasets into insights that change how we lend. You'll own your work end-to-end: from framing the question and pulling the data through to modelling, presenting a recommendation and seeing it live in our decision engine. You'll be working with a small team and a modern stack, alongside a Head of Credit who has built this function from scratch and who will give you real ownership from day one. This is not a role where you hand models over a wall and move on - you'll see the impact of your decisions immediately. What you'll be doing Build, validate and monitor application and behavioural scorecards, using bureau, Open Banking and internal data to improve how we assess new-to-UK and thin-file customers. Design, test and refine our credit strategy: cut-offs, affordability rules, pricing tiers and limits, with a clear view of the trade-off between risk, volume and margin. Run experiments and champion/challenge tests to prove that changes to policy and models actually work before we scale them. Explore new data sources and alternative signals, and build the case for using (or not using) them in decisioning. Support model governance: document what you build, evidence that it treats customers fairly, and help us meet our Consumer Duty, CONC and model risk obligations. Work with our engineers to get models and rules into production

jobs.description: <p><strong>What we are looking for:</strong></p> <p>We are building the live-service meta for an upcoming game, and three of its most important systems do not yet have a principal design owner: the events that give the game a weekly heartbeat, the social structures that make progression something players do together rather than alone, and the onboarding that has to teach both. This role owns the first two outright and is the design partner on the third.</p> <p>This is a design, maintain, and iterate role. Our event event architecture, our LiveOps operating model, and our community structures are about to be defined. You would be the person driving those and designing them, alongside the other Designers, PM and UX team.</p> <p>This is a fully remote, principal-level individual contributor role on the Meta &amp; Live Service team, reporting to the Design Director, Meta &amp; Live Service.</p> <p>&nbsp;</p> <p><strong>What we will do together:</strong></p> <p><span style="text-decoration: underline;"><strong>Events and LiveOps design systems</strong></span></p> <ul> <li>Design events: a growing set of reusable, configurable formats that scale to a meet our audience needs.</li> <li>Design events end to end: entry conditions, currencies, consumables, reward pacing, and how events feed and are fed by the wider meta rather than sitting beside it.</li> <li>Assist in defining the configuration surfaces and tooling requirements that make running an event a config job rather than an engineering job.</li> <li>Help set the standard for how events are specced, instrumented, reviewed and iterated after they run, and retired.</li> </ul> <p>&nbsp;</p> <p><span style="text-decoration: underline;"><strong>Social and community systems</strong></span></p> <ul> <li>Design various community and social systems that will help curate a strong community that grows together.&nbsp;</li> <li>Partner with the various teams to see how each feature can be added to a social layer.</li> <li>Design the end-to-end social funnel experience</li> </ul> <p>&nbsp;</p> <p><span style="text-decoration: underline;"><strong>Onboarding partnership</strong></span></p> <ul> <li>Partner with the FTUE pod and designer to sequence meta systems into onboarding</li> <li>Define nudge, notification and re-entry logic, including the return path for lapsed players.</li> <li>Help define the telemetry that tells us whether onboarding taught what it was supposed to teach.</li> </ul> <p>&nbsp;</p> <p><strong>What you will bring:</strong></p> <ul> <li>8+ years in game design, including 4+ years designing for and operating a live-service title after launch. Post-launch operating experience matters more here than shipping experience.</li> <li>Demonstrated ownership of event systems, social systems, or both, on a title you supported live, not only specced.</li> <li>Fluency in progression and economy design. jobs.description: <h2>🧡 About Alma</h2> <p>At Alma, we believe sustainable commerce depends on fair, well-balanced trade. Because finance plays a pivotal role in business, our mission is to put it back in its rightful place — serving merchants and consumers.</p> <p>Our installment and deferred payment solutions help merchants boost sales by 20% or more, increase customer loyalty, and deliver a seamless shopping experience — without encouraging bad debt.</p> <p>As the buy now pay later leader in France and active in 10 European countries, we've empowered over +25,000 merchants and 10 million consumers.</p> <p>With 380+ Almakers and €100M+ ARR in 2025, Alma is scaling rapidly across Europe as a member of the Next40, and we're just getting started!</p> <h2>👐 About the team</h2> <p>Alma is a lender. We originate several million consumer receivables a year, carry them for a few weeks, and refinance them off a deliberately light balance sheet through securitization vehicles (Fonds Communs de Titrisation) and our other funding lines. We are regulated as a société de financement and a payment institution.</p> <p>That changes what "accounting" means here. A lender's accounts are not a monthly deliverable produced at the end of a chain: <strong>they are the chain</strong>. Every payment event, every commission, every provision, every sale of receivables to an FCT has to become a journal entry that ties — to the transaction underneath it, to the general ledger above it, and to the prudential statements the regulator reads. At our scale and growth, this is a strategic topic, and one that is as much about data as it is about accounting.</p> <p>Today the chain exists: an internal core banking ledger we built ourselves, feeding NetSuite, feeding regulatory reporting. What it does not have is a single owner who understands it end-to-end, holds it to the standard a regulated lender needs, and evolves it as the business changes (geographies, products, licenses). That is the role we are opening.</p> <p>You will join an Accounting team inside a Finance organization of ~15 people covering Strategic Financing, FP&amp;A, Accounting, Regulatory reporting and Controlling. You will report to the Head of Financing &amp; Accounting, alongside the Financing team and the General Accounting Manager, who oversees corporate cycles, tax, statutory and consolidated accounts.</p> <p>This is a role with unusual ownership for its level: the banking accounting scope is yours from day one, and so is the data chain that produces it.</p> <h2>💼 About the job</h2> <p><strong>Own the accounting of the credit business:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Own how the portfolio is represented in the books: origination, revenue recognition on merchant and customer commissions, deferred income, write-offs and recoveries, cost of risk and provisioning on performing and non-performing exposures.</li> <li>Own the accounting of our securitizations: sales of receivables to the FCTs, derecognition, discount and over-collateralisation, residual interests, servicing and management fees, hedging.</li> <li>Own the accounting of our funding: corporate debt, commercial paper, and the new funding instruments we add as the refinancing strategy evolves.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Own the core banking ledger:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Be the functional owner of the engine that turns business events into accounting: which event, which account, which currency, which date, which counterparty.</li> <li>Specify and validate the accounting schemes for every new product, partner and geography, and work with Engineering and Data on the ledger's model, its feed into the ERP, and the fixes when something drifts.</li> <li>Own

jobs.description: Chez Lifen, nous pensons que les données médicales ont le potentiel de transformer le système de santé. Mais seulement si elles sont accessibles. Plus de données accessibles → moins de charge administrative, une meilleure coordination des soins et des découvertes scientifiques plus rapides. Depuis 2015, notre mission est de libérer ce potentiel. Nos solutions basées sur l'IA permettent aux professionnels de santé de partager les informations médicales sans effort et aux chercheurs d'accélérer les découvertes cliniques : avec un impact sur des millions de patients en France chaque jour. Alors que nous nous préparons à nous développer en Europe, deux choses déterminent notre succès : nos équipes et notre mission. Aujourd'hui, plus de 150 personnes travaillent depuis nos bureaux et à distance pour libérer le potentiel des données de santé. Nous avons connecté 800 hôpitaux et 150 000 professionnels de santé, et nous ne faisons que commencer. Nous recherchons des personnes qui embrassent la complexité, veulent résoudre des problèmes difficiles et sont prêtes à construire le futur de la collaboration en santé. 🧩 Notre équipe Customer Operations Chez Lifen, nous déployons nos solutions dans les hôpitaux de toute la France pour améliorer le quotidien des soignants et la qualité des soins. L'équipe Customer Operations est le pont entre nos produits et les établissements de santé. Elle accompagne chaque hôpital dans l'implémentation de nos solutions : Lifen Documents & Lifen Intégration. Notre équipe est composée de Project Managers et d'Operations Managers, tous pilotés par Loïc, notre Lead Customer Operations. Nous recherchons aujourd'hui un profil à la croisée de la technique et de la gestion de projet : une personne capable de piloter un déploiement client de bout en bout, mais aussi de prendre en main les aspects techniques de l'intégration de nos solutions. Si tu aimes autant comprendre comment fonctionnent les systèmes informatiques que coordonner les parties prenantes d'un projet, ce poste devrait te plaire ! 🎯 Ce que tu feras chez nous En tant que Technical Implementation Manager, tu seras responsable de la mise en œuvre technique de nos solutions dans les établissements de santé, depuis le cadrage initial jusqu'à leur mise en production. Ton rôle ? Faire en sorte que nos solutions s'intègrent correctement dans les systèmes d'information hospitaliers, tout en garantissant le bon déroulement des déploiements. jobs.title: First RevOps
jobs.description: At Parallel, we build AI agents to help healthcare facilities automate their administrative processes and unlock additional revenue, starting with medical coding. Today, up to 25% of healthcare spending is lost in manual, repetitive administrative work. Legacy software hasn’t helped, it’s made things slower, more complex, and more frustrating for care teams. We believe AI agents can change that. Our technology combines Large Language Models with system-level automation to handle real work inside existing hospital tools. No integrations, no disruption. Our first agent automates coding workflows and frees up time for medical staff to focus on patients. We launched in 2024, are backed by top investors (Index, Frst, Y Combinator, Hexa, Kima Ventures, Better Angle), and we’re just getting started. The future of healthcare isn’t just digital — it’s automated. Come help us build it ! Context Our coding agent is live in 70 hospitals across France. In March, we raised $20M from Index Ventures to push it further and build what comes next: billing, admissions, patient records. The next six months are going to move fast. We'll double to +60 people, open Germany, and triple the size of our Revenue team. Today, too much of how we run the company still depends on manual work and tools that don't talk to each other. Nobody owns this problem yet, it will be yours. Your mission Make sure Parallel can double without drowning in manual work. Attio, our CRM, will be your main tool, and you'll run it end to end. You'll also sit with each team, see what they still do by hand, and automate it yourself. On top of that, you'll work on Sales, Marketing and Finance Ops topics, like billing, cash tracking and commissions. You'll report to Clem, our Ops Lead, and work every day with the founders and the go-to-market teams. You build things, you don't write decks about them. There's no team to manage at first, but the function is yours to shape, and we assume it will grow. What you'll do Own Attio, end to end Administer and configure Attio: data model, pipelines, fields, views, access rights and workflows Enrich our CRM with data valuable for Sales, Ops and Finance teams, so that it can be the source of truth while scaling Connect Attio to the rest of our stack so processes run without manual steps Support users and turn their pain points into better configurations Automate our internal work, with AI where it makes sense Map repetitive tasks across Sales, Marketing, Ops and Finance, and prioritize them by impact and effort Build automations, integrations and AI use cases yourself, with no-code or low-code tools, and APIs when needed Pick a simple rule or AI depending on the need, test on real cases, and keep a human in the loop when it matters Protect sensitive data, control access, and measure time saved, errors and costs Make Sales and Ops steering reliable Help define the priority metrics and agree on shared definitions Run the analyses, SQL queries and dashboards yourself Automate data collection and updates to kill manual reporting Build processes that hold as we double Document the rules, owners, limits of AI use and what to do when something breaks Structure the handoffs between teams, train users and check real adoption in the field Outcomes You ship from week one: automations are expected in your first month, not in six. Month 1: diagnose and ship a first win You run Attio autonomously, have audited its configuration and data, and shipped the first improvements teams feel A prioritized list of automation and AI opportunities, and a 90-day plan validated with Clem Your first automation is live, tested with its users, with a baseline measured to track the gain Month 2: deploy and measure Several automations are used by the teams, with time saved and output quality tracked on real cases Priority metrics are live and tested with the teams Month 3: stabilize and drive adoption Several automations run in production, used regularly, with error monitoring

Every organization can license the same AI models, but no two organizations share the same institutional knowledge. Decades of experience, work product, and precedent are often fragmented across systems, underused, and inaccessible. DeepJudge makes this expertise instantly available and actionable – helping legal teams find the right information faster, surface relevant knowledge, and apply it where it matters most. Our platform is trusted by many of the world’s leading law firms and legal teams, including Holland & Knight, Gunderson Dettmer, Cozen O’Connor, ArentFox Schiff, CMS Switzerland, Schoenherr, and others. Headquartered in Switzerland with a growing team across North America and Europe, DeepJudge is shaping the future of how professional knowledge is discovered and applied. At DeepJudge, we move with urgency, think rigorously, and work closely with our clients to build products that solve meaningful problems. If you want to help define how AI transforms professional knowledge work, we’d love to hear from you. About the role: We’re looking for a Revenue Operations Manager to strengthen the systems that power our go-to-market teams. This is a builder role for someone who can design, implement, and own the processes, workflows, automations, and data architecture that accelerate how we find, engage, win, onboard, retain, and expand customers at scale. You will partner across Marketing, Sales, Customer Success, and Partnership to turn fragmented systems and manual work into a high-leverage GTM engine. If you naturally think: “This should be an automated system, not a spreadsheet.” …you’ll likely be a strong fit. We would love to connect with you about enabling our rapidly growing revenue team. You will play a key role in increasing internal efficiency and productivity to support the team in creating the best customer experience, and in driving commercial success. Your responsibilities will include: CRM and revenue tech stack architecture Own end-to-end CRM administration as the single source of truth for revenue activities Manage the design, configuration, and roadmap of a connected revenue tech stack Set and enforce data governance standards: field hygiene, deduplication, permissions, and ongoing data-quality monitoring Automation and data foundation Automate and enrich the manual layer with workflows and LLMs Build and maintain operational dashboards (recurring KPIs, data hygiene, system adoption) Advise with thought leadership on which tooling we procure next as we scale Cross-functional partnership and enablement Operational business partner to GTM leadership Drive systems and process adoption across Marketing, Sales, Customer Success, and Partnership teams through training and enablement Act as first point of contact for revenue system support tickets What success looks like in 12 months: GTM signals are consistently translated into actionable workflows Sellers and customer-facing teams spend materially less time on manual admin and prep Critical revenue systems are connected, key workflows are AI-assisted or fully automated Leadership has a real-time view into pipeline, conversion, execution, and customer health You're a great fit if you: 5+ years in Revenue/Sales Operations in a B2B SaaS hypergrowth environment Deep hands-on expertise in CRM administration (HubSpot/Salesforce) Proven track record building revenue systems, processes, and data flows from scratch Persistent problem-solver at your core Sharp entrepreneurial instincts and analytical mindset Excellent cross-functional stakeholder management What you can look forward to: Taking full ownership

jobs.title: Solution Consultant - R&D
jobs.description: We are rebuilding biotech for the AI era. When a breakthrough is delayed, the world waits. Getting a molecule from discovery to patients, or a crop from lab to field, involves thousands of slow, manual, disconnected steps. AI has the potential to change this, compressing decades of R&D work into years. But that only happens when clean, structured scientific data and AI are built into how science gets done. Benchling is the AI platform for biotech R&D. Scientists use Benchling to design experiments, capture structured data, and run AI agents and models directly in their workflows. Over 200,000 scientists around the world trust Benchling to power their most important work, from academic labs to Sanofi, Moderna, and more than half of the world's top 50 biopharma. We’re building an AI scientist for our customers. We can’t do that if we haven’t built the muscle ourselves. AI fluency is the foundation we build on; it's core to how we work, and we're committed to helping every new hire integrate it into their day-to-day. As part of our interview process, you'll complete a brief AI-focused exercise or discussion so we can understand how you think about and use AI to drive impact in your role. Feel free to reference any tools, platforms, or workflows you use today. ROLE OVERVIEW Benchling Solution Consultants (SC) are the primary solution leads with Benchling’s largest customers and prospects. Their solutions are deployed into complex enterprise IT environments, interfacing with other vendor solutions, lab instruments, and legacy applications. This is a highly visible role that partners with both external and internal teams to develop the optimal solutions that drive the most value for our customers. The SC is a pre-sales role, and as such works closely with Benchling sales leadership, account executives, professional services, and product leaders to ensure the best solutions are presented. SCs work with senior scientific and IT leaders from prospects and customers, to establish credibility and confidence from the first meeting, and to create solutions based on cutting-edge technologies. The SC must be comfortable with Life Sciences R&D processes and scientific concepts, have experience with enterprise SaaS solutions, and be adept at working with internal and external leaders and stakeholders. You must work as a trusted adviser to translate customer objectives into detailed solutions and effectively communicate and demonstrate those solutions to prospects and customers. RESPONSIBILITIES Effectively partner with account executives, SC peers, and leadership to create account and deal strategies that lead to selection, planning out customer engagements that lead to compelling solutions. Manage organized discoveries to uncover customer needs and requirements that relate to decision criteria and key business issues. Craft solutions based on Benchling capabilities, industry best practices and standard R&D functions, with data models and processes that map to the customer or prospects' science and that fit into their current technology landscape. Present and demonstrate the solution in a persuasive way based on key messages, decision criteria, and key business issues. Manage customer questions and objections and resolve concerns. Ensure that the solution is presented competitively, with awareness of alternatives including build in house. Engage with product management to provide insight into prospect and customer needs and industry trends. Influence the roadmap for market success. Ensure that the roadmap is clear to customers as required to influence buying decisions. Provide leadership by creating reusable solutions, content, and trainings for key areas. Work with the extended team to ensure that they are successful and learn from your expertise. Mentor and partner with other SCs to build their success. jobs.description: Description Legartis is on a mission: to unlock legal work at scale. We set the standard for AI-powered contract work by offering a platform that changes how legal teams work, from drafting through negotiation to completion. We are now looking for the person who turns what customers actually need into what our AI actually does. Joining Legartis is not taking a job, you take ownership. We are a team of product builders and lawyers, who do not chase hype; we build substance. If you are a lawyer who builds, someone who has stopped waiting for better tools and started making them, this is your moment and your place. Send us your CV, a short note on why Legartis, and links to anything you have built or published. Your mission Most companies split this seat across three teams, and that split is exactly the problem. The person who hears the customer describe their workflow should be the person who writes the requirement, and the person who writes the requirement should be able to build the first version themselves. That is you. 1. You translate customer reality into engineering requirements — and into revenue. You sit in customer and expert calls alongside Sales, not as a note-taker but as the person who understands the legal work. In trials and hackathons you coach hands-on: the customer drives, you navigate, and they create the first "wow" moment themselves. When they say "that won't work for us" or "we'll build it ourselves", you answer with a concrete path (a workaround, a workflow, the honest maintenance cost of the alternative) and you leave every conversation with a next step: trial licenses, a hackathon, a scoped rollout. Then you pull out the workflow: what actually happens, in what order, where it breaks, what the customer would pay to never do again. And you write the spec, edge cases, and acceptance criteria that Engineering can build against. 2. You build the skills yourself. You write, test, and ship agent skills and playbooks that solve real customer workflows. You build the evaluation frameworks and test sets that prove they got better rather than just different. When the AI fails on a clause, you diagnose why, at the prompt and context level, and you either fix it or hand Engineering a diagnosis precise enough to act on. 3. You make it repeatable, and therefore sellable. Anything you build once for one customer, you turn into something Sales and Customer Success can run without you. Standard demo environments. A skill library they can reach for. Onboarding that lands in days rather than months. Where Customer Success needs legal depth you step in, fix it, and turn the fix into something the team can handle alone next time. Your success is measured by how rarely you need to be in the room, and by what happens to adoption and expansion when you are not. 4. You are the legal authority in the building. Legal and compliance questions land with you: contract reviews, customer security and data protection questions, the occasional in-house matter which makes roughly ten to fifteen percent of your time. You use our own product to do it, and you tell us honestly when it is not good enough. Your profile The person we picture. There is a name emerging for what we are describing, and it is not "lawyer who is good with computers". It is legal quant : a lawyer who builds their own tooling to practise law, rather than waiting for a vendor to ship it. The distinction that matters to us: plenty of lawyers now use AI. A legal quant builds with it. They look at a workflow and ask how to redesign it from first principles to get the best possible outcome, rather than making the existing process incrementally faster. A note on how we are weighting this role. Three capabilities make someone exceptional here: commercial instinct, legal depth, and technical ability to build. The ideal candidate has all three. jobs.description: About ElevenLabs ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology. We launched in January 2023 with the first human-like AI voice model. Today, we serve millions of users and thousands of businesses - from fast-growing startups to large enterprises like Deutsche Telekom and Meta. Our investors are some of the world's most prominent, including Andreessen Horowitz, ICONIQ Growth and Sequoia. We've raised $781M in funding and our last valuation was $22B - multiples of 11, always. ElevenAPI gives developers access to our leading AI audio foundational models. Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you. AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location. jobs.title: Senior Data Scientist
jobs.description: Who We Are Hi, we're DuckDuckGo, the online protection company and remote-first team of 300+ on a mission to raise the standard of trust online. Founded in 2008 and profitable since 2014, annual revenue now exceeds $100m USD and millions use our browser on on Mac , Windows , iOS , and Android , our search engine , and the DuckDuckGo subscription . We also offer private, useful, and optional AI, including Duck.ai , which lets you chat privately with ChatGPT, Claude, and other AIs, all in one place. Our culture of trust, inclusivity, and empowered project management underpins everything we do, where each team member takes full ownership of their projects, from scoping and execution to postmortem. If you're seeking end-to-end ownership of your work, you've come to the right place! Your Team and Role Working on the Data Science Functional Team, you'll drive product and business impact through statistical modeling, experiment design, Bayesian marketing analysis, and classifier implementation across our search engine, instant answers, AI, and revenue optimization, and work on related projects. Recent projects include: Defining core growth metrics for our products and building the infrastructure to monitor trends and anomalies Measuring the impact of major marketing campaigns for Duck.ai , translating full-funnel data into actionable decisions Building monitoring pipelines to detect unexpected shifts in search traffic patterns faster and more reliably Expanding evaluation datasets for page context understanding across complex scenarios like multi-tab browsing and content reattachment Improving the trigger systems that determine when AI-assisted answers surface in DuckDuckGo Search, balancing quality and our privacy-first approach Our data meets rigorous privacy standards and is necessarily sparse, so you'll need to think creatively to surface actionable insights in an evidence-first culture where quantitative rigor is the baseline, not the exception. About You You have 7+ years of experience in Data Science and a track record of leading high-complexity projects from scoping to production with minimal direction. You can do 2 or more of the following: Deploy and iterate on ML in production environments Develop and deploy NLP solutions Apply knowledge of LLMs including fine-tuning, LLM-as-judge, and AI-assisted development Conduct marketing campaign analysis using Bayesian methods You write production-grade code in Python or a comparable high-level language. You have advanced SQL and query optimization skills, familiarity with columnar databases like BigQuery, Clickhouse, Redshift, or Druid; experience with a BI tool like Tableau or PowerBI is a plus. You can design, implement, and analyze experiments across product surfaces, and are comfortable deriving insights from sparse or privacy-constrained data. You collaborate effectively with product teams and contribute to overall team throughput. Compensation $178,500 USD annually and stock options. Compensation is transparent across the organization, and all team members within the same professional level and global region receive the same compensation. Eligibility for company-sponsored health benefits is limited to team members based in the United States. This program does not extend to team members located in other countries, such as Canada or the UK. Our Team Member Support Guide explains how we prioritize your wellbeing including paid parental leave, office setup, and co-working allowances. jobs.title: Software Engineer, Robot Autonomy, Intern
jobs.description: Our Mission At Laelaps AI, we believe robotics is entering a transformative decade, much like the arrival of the internet. Advances in AI, cloud computing, and hardware are reshaping what autonomous systems can do. Our mission is to build the intelligent software that powers physical security in the real world - enabling robots and sensors to handle dangerous and critical tasks that humans shouldn't have to. By engineering the orchestration layer for intelligent security, we aim to create a world that is safer, more secure, and more resilient. We're a strong founding team based in Zurich, backed by visionary investors and advisors. We are engineering the future of security today! The Role As a Software Engineer intern on Robot Autonomy, you'll work on the software that runs on our legged security robots: how they perceive their surroundings, know where they are, and move through real customer sites on patrol. You'll join the team that owns everything on the robot and take a well-scoped problem from first experiment to a result that runs on hardware. The role focuses on building software for the robot autonomy stack that runs in the field. We'll agree your focus area with you during the interview process, based on your strengths and the team's priorities, and we expect you to own it from day one. This role is hands-on. You'll work with real sensor data and field logs, test on physical robots, and see first-hand why a robot that works in the lab can still fail on a live site at night, in rain, or after the layout changes. What You'll Work On Build and improve components of the on-robot autonomy stack, such as perception, localisation and state estimation, or planning and navigation, depending on your background and the team's priorities. Integrate sensors such as lidar, cameras and IMU, and work with the data they produce in day, night and challenging weather. Reproduce issues from field deployments using logs and simulation, find the root cause, and help fix it at the right layer. Design repeatable tests and clear metrics that show whether a change holds up across routes, lighting, weather and site layouts. Test your work on physical robots, and join site visits to see how the system behaves in real operating conditions. Apply solid engineering practices: code review, version control, reproducible experiments and clear documentation. Who We're Looking For We're looking for a strong robotics student who wants to see their work run on real robots, not only in simulation. You don't need every item below, but you should meet the core requirements and bring depth in at least one area of the autonomy stack. You'll join a small team that moves fast, expects ownership, and holds work to the standard of running on live customer sites. Your Background Currently pursuing a Master's or PhD, or completed a Master's degree within the last year, in Robotics, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering or a closely related field. Demonstrated depth in at least one of perception, localisation and state estimation, or motion planning and navigation, through a thesis, research or a substantial project. Strong coding skills in Python. Hands-on experience with ROS 2. Comfortable using Linux, Docker and Git in your workflows. Nice to Have Experience working with physical robots, ideally mobile or legged. Experience with lidar or camera processing, SLAM, or sensor fusion. Experience with robotics simulators such as Isaac Sim, Gazebo or MuJoCo. Publications or competition results in robotics (ICRA, IROS, RSS, CoRL). What We Offer Ownership: you are able to ship products and deliver project end-to-end. Mission: autonomous security that keeps people and critical sites safe, including in defence. Career path: a ground-floor seat with real runway. Prove your value and you will not have barriers to grow. Team: work directly with PhD-level co-founders in AI, Robotics, and Physics, alongside a strong (and fun) founding team. Compensation: Competitive equity/sal

Our platform connects employees worldwide to the best partners for fitness, mindfulness, therapy, nutrition, and sleep—all in one simple subscription. Headquartered in NYC with team members in Europe, North America and South America, we’re on a mission to make every company a wellness company.</p> <p>We believe work should be fulfilling, inspiring, and balanced. Here, you’ll find a team that values wellbeing, collaboration, and different perspectives, where passion and creativity push boundaries to create real impact. Your contributions will help shape a healthier, more balanced world for you and millions of people globally.&nbsp;</p> <p><strong>Join us in redefining the future of wellbeing!</strong></p> <p>&nbsp;</p> <p><strong>THE OPPORTUNITY</strong></p> <p>We are hiring a <strong>People Operations Working Student</strong> to our <strong>People Operations</strong> team in <strong>Berlin</strong>!</p> <p>This role is to join our People Operations team, dedicated to delivering an exceptional employee experience across Europe. In this role, you will contribute to meaningful People initiatives and gain valuable exposure to key HR topics including employment law, payroll, and HR systems (e.g., Personio), all within a fast-paced, international environment</p> <p>&nbsp;</p> <p><strong>YOUR IMPACT</strong></p> <ul> <li>Address and resolve employee queries with clarity and care by guiding them to the right resources.</li> <li>Support payroll processing by accurately entering and validating HR data in a timely manner.</li> <li>Assist with internal audits, documentation, and the gathering of key compliance information.</li> <li>Maintain accurate HR data in Personio and support reporting to inform data-driven decision-making.</li> <li>Contribute to process optimization and strategic People projects spanning the entire employee lifecycle, including onboarding and offboarding.</li> <li>Live the mission: inspire and empower others by genuinely caring for your own wellbeing and your colleagues. Bring wellbeing to the forefront of work, and create a supportive environment where everyone feels comfortable taking care of themselves, taking time off, and finding work-life wellness.</li> </ul> <p><strong>WHO YOU ARE</strong></p> <ul> <li>A university student currently enrolled in HR, Business, or a related discipline, available to work between 15 and 20 hours per week.</li> <li>A fluent communicator with C1+ level proficiency in both written and spoken German and English.</li> <li>A Berlin-based candidate who can work on-site from our Head Office 2–3 times per week.</li> <li>A discreet professional with a proven ability to handle confidential and sensitive information with high integrity.</li> <li>A self-driven, adaptable, and collaborative team player with excellent organizational skills and strong attention to detail.</li> <li>A proactive learner passionate about employee experience, eager to develop skills in project management, stakeholder management, and HR operations across Europe.</li> </ul> <p>We recognize that individuals approach job applications differently. jobs.title: Supply Chain Planning Working Student (all genders)
jobs.description: <h2><strong>Your role</strong></h2> <p>We are looking for a Supply Chain planning working student for 12 months at the heart of our Product team, where you will be responsible for supporting our operational and strategic needs for our physical product: meal kits. You will be central to our activity and will have a significant influence on our customers' meals.</p> <p>We are looking for someone capable of assisting us in the operational planning of recipes at HelloFresh. This is a unique opportunity to learn and gain experience within a fast-growing company that is pioneering the food industry.</p> <p>If you want to be a driving force in the growth of a scale-up, then this position is for you!</p> <p>&nbsp;</p> <h2><strong>Your area of responsibility</strong></h2> <ul> <li><strong>Menu creation and optimization: </strong>Assist the team in creating and optimizing menus using our python-based menu-planning algorithm.</li> <li><strong>Product Improvement:</strong> You will work on several projects and initiatives that focus on improving our product offering aiming to increase customer satisfaction.</li> <li><strong>Menu De-Risking:</strong> You will lead a number of cross-collaborative initiatives and processes aiming to reduce the menu risk and to ensure ingredient availability by considering the end-to-end value chain of our product.&nbsp;</li> <li><strong>Operations support:</strong> You support the team in day-to-day operations as well as with administrative and organizational tasks along the supply and menu planning process and have the opportunity to solve concrete problems, make decisions, and learn to manage real-world situations in a dynamic environment.</li> <li><strong>Process management:</strong> You will participate in projects aimed at optimizing and automating and improving our product processes and supply chain by working with other teams.</li> <li><strong>Reporting:</strong> You will track the weekly performance of menus and recipes, and conduct analyses on their monthly/quarterly performance.</li> <li><strong>Recipe change management in menus:</strong> You will select alternative recipes when needed (ingredient shortage, marketing need, etc.).</li> <li><strong>Recipe &amp; Ingredient Pool management:</strong> You will contribute to the maintenance of the recipe and ingredient database in alignment with the culinary teams.</li> <li><strong>Customization: </strong>You will support the expansion of our product offering by uploading and managing customized menu options to provide customers with greater choice.</li> </ul> <p>&nbsp;</p> <h2><strong>Your profile</strong></h2> <ul> <li>You are completing a degree in Business Administration, Management, Industrial Engineering, or a related discipline, ideally with a focus on Product Management, Supply Chain or Operations Management.</li> <li>Initial experience in product management or supply planning, CPG and E-Commerce experience is a plus.</li> <li>Excellent command of Excel; jobs.title: Senior CRM Manager - Transformation (all genders)
jobs.description: <h2><strong>The role</strong></h2> <p>We are looking for a <em>Senior CRM Manager - Transformation </em>to make CRM Self-Service at HelloFresh a reality.</p> <p>Our central <em>Growth </em>function has a clear vision: Enabling our local marketing and product teams to reach our customers directly, via push notifications, in-app messaging and emails. For this to work in an efficient and customer-centric way, the right guardrails, tools and knowledge need to be in place.</p> <p>Your first mission is to design, launch and scale our CRM self-service model. You’ll do this hand in hand with our CreativeTech squad (Product and Engineering), who are building the future CRM environment in an AI-native way. You’ll work closely with the squad, and potentially be embedded in it. You’ll be the voice of CRM and of our internal users, helping define what this environment needs to look like so teams can send communications safely and independently.</p> <p>This is 0-to-1 work in a highly ambiguous space where no one has been before: no playbook, no rules. AI and LLMs change fast and often, so you’ll think about what we need in the future, even if today’s models aren’t ready yet, and be prepared for when they catch up. The learning curve will be steep, but you’ll climb it on the go, together with the team. Our goal: protect our environment from the agents, and protect the agents from our environment.&nbsp;</p> <p>From there, your focus will follow where CRM needs it most. You’ll take on further transformation projects, so this role is for someone who enjoys building something new and then moving on to the next challenge.</p> <p>Above all, we are looking for people who will&nbsp;<strong>make HelloFresh</strong>&nbsp;<strong>better.</strong>&nbsp;We believe there are many different ways of developing skills and we love diverse experiences! So even if you don’t “tick all the boxes” but think you’d thrive in this role, we would really like to learn more about you.</p> <h2><strong>What you’ll do</strong></h2> <ul> <li><strong>Lead the self-service rollout:</strong> Take end-to-end ownership of the programme, from framing the scope and aligning stakeholders to launching and tracking adoption</li> <li><strong>Shape the future CRM platform:</strong> Collaborate with Product and Engineering to define how our agentic CRM environment should work, bringing in the needs of users and helping prioritise what gets built next&nbsp;</li> <li><strong>Steer CRM Agents: </strong>Build the skills and context agents need to create campaigns reliably, on brand and within our guardrails&nbsp;</li> <li><strong>Build frameworks and playbooks:</strong> Develop the documentation, training and processes that let teams send safely without central support</li> <li><strong>Enable the teams:</strong> Design and run user centric training and onboarding for local marketing and product teams, and turn user feedback into improvements</li> <li><strong>Make performance visible:</strong> Define and create reportings to measure success</li> <li><strong>Scale what works:</strong> Identify new use cases to move to self-service and manage each transition end to end</li> <li><strong>Drive the next CRM initiatives: </strong>Once self-service is established, take ownership of further cross-functional projects that make our CRM team more scalable and efficient</li> <li><strong>Modernize processes with AI:</strong> Collaborate with the CreativeTech squad and CRM Operations to adapt AI use cases within our CRM workflows&nbsp;</li> <li><strong>Influence the CRM product roadm

jobs.title: Principal Security Engineer, Security Tribe
jobs.description: <h2><strong>The role</strong></h2> <p>We are looking for a <strong>Principal Security Engineer</strong> to serve as one of HelloFresh's most senior technical authorities in Security — shaping how we protect the company today while defining the security foundations we will need for the future.</p> <p>This is not a Principal role defined by ownership of a single security domain. <strong>Your domain is HelloFresh.</strong></p> <p>You will operate at the intersection of <strong>technology strategy, security architecture, engineering and business risk</strong>, influencing some of the most consequential technical decisions we make. Your main goal will be to make it simple and reliable for customers to buy, pay for, and grow their use of n8n. You'll own the foundations of how n8n's commercial system works: licensing and entitlements, customer accounts, and the metering and billing platform for both Cloud and Enterprise. Introduce "account" as a first-class product primitive (accounts, purchases, license keys, activations) and expose it as the API contract our customer-facing console and multi-instance management are built on. Productize the deal-to-entitlement flow so a closed deal in Salesforce creates or updates entitlements without manual steps. METERING & BILLING PLATFORM Own usage metering and billing for Cloud and Enterprise, including subscription billing: what counts as a billable execution, quota consumption, and overage charging. Lead the migration off Paddle Classic and unify Cloud and Enterprise billing into one platform. Build the mechanics for usage-based enterprise billing and reliable overage charging. CROSS-ORG ALIGNMENT Make the architecture and mechanism decisions (entitlement model, billing platform, enterprise invoicing path) and align closely with Finance and go-to-market on each of them. Every decision here touches money; you bring people along rather than inform them afterwards. Hold clear boundaries with adjacent teams: the customer console, execution limits, and access control live elsewhere; you own the data and mechanics they rely on. Establish clear success measures and keep the squad accountable for outcomes, not only delivery. REQUIREMENTS Must-haves Billing or licensing product experience

jobs.title: Executive Assistant
jobs.description: 🌍 About Outpost Global expansion is broken. Without a local entity, conversion rates fall, costs rise, and compliance gets messy. Outpost fixes it. Outpost is your modular back office for global commerce. Pick only what you need - tax, payments, treasury, or operations - and unlock new markets without the overhead. Sometimes we act as Merchant of Record, taking on tax and compliance risk. Other times, we give you the tools to do it yourself. Sell anything, anywhere. Without compromise. 🧠 The Role We're hiring a second Executive Assistant to support our CEO. We already have an EA, and she isn't going anywhere. You'll report to the CEO and work alongside her: she keeps inbound, customer routing and the investor-facing side, takes diary, travel, logistics, internal admin, and hiring coordination. You'll join to take a defined set of workstreams off that plate. Roughly 70% of this role is executive support. The other 30% is hiring - and that's where the leverage is. We run a five-stage interview loop across engineering, ops, product, GTM and tax, hiring around two people a month. Someone needs to own the machinery: scheduling across five calendars and four countries, keeping candidates warm, chasing feedback, making sure nobody good goes cold because a diary didn't line up. This is a role for someone early in their career who is unusually organised and wants to learn how a company actually gets built. You won't be handed a finished process. You'll be shown how we do things today, and expected to make it better. 🧩 What You'll Do Own the CEO's diary and logistics Run scheduling day to day - booking, moving, protecting focus time, resolving clashes before they become problems Book and manage international travel, and rebuild it when a flight moves Prepare meeting packs: who's in the room, what they want, what happened last time Track and chase the follow-ups nobody wrote down Do the work he never sees The highest-value work here is invisible. He shouldn't know it happened - he should just find the day went smoothly Fix problems before they reach him: the double-booking, the missing dial-in, the visa that needed renewing Do the quiet prep - background on a person he's meeting, what was agreed last time, the numbers checked before a deck goes out Anticipate. If a trip is booked, the transfer, the dinner and the buffer around the flight are already handled The fewer questions he has to ask you, the better you're doing the job Own hiring coordination Run scheduling across the full interview loop - five stages, multiple interviewers, several time zones Keep the pipeline clean: trackers, interview feedback, stage-by-stage conversion Build target lists for open roles and help manage outreach Be the candidate's point of contact - fast, warm, human. How we treat candidates is how we're judged Coordinate offers, references, contracts, start dates, and new-hire onboarding logistics Keep the company running Support board and investor prep alongside the CEO, Chief of Staff and our senior EA Help run internal comms: all-hands, offsites, company updates Manage supplier, tooling and expense admin so nobody else has to think about it Spot the recurring problem and fix it permanently rather than solving it again next week 💥 Example Projects Rebuild a full week of CEO travel in an afternoon after a fundraising meeting moves Take time-to-offer from three weeks to ten days by fixing scheduling and feedback bottlenecks Build the candidate tracker that shows conversion at every interview stage, and run it weekly Own the logistics for a board meeting: pre-reads, agenda, materials, follow-ups Organise a company offsite for a team split across London, Amsterdam and beyond Write down how you do your job so the next person can pick it up in a week 🧱 What We're Looking For Ideal background: 1–3 years in an EA, team assistant, recruiting coordinator or ops support role - ideally at a startup or fast-growing tech / fintech company Any recruiting coordination expos

jobs.title: Strategic Finance
jobs.description: Metaview is an AI company focused on recruiting. We build AI agents that help world-class companies hire with radically more speed and precision. We automate the toil, and augment the human for companies like Brex, Affirm, Deel, ElevenLabs, and Airtable. Founded by Siadhal and Shahriar after their experiences scaling Uber and Palantir, we’ve raised $110m from top-tier investors including Google Ventures and Insight Partners. It's still day 0: Now is the time to re-engineer how work gets done with AI at the core, and our toughest challenges still lie ahead. We're looking for people seeking the hardest, most fulfilling work of their lives. How we work Four principles guide us: Velocity. Optimize for rate of learning. Take action, get feedback, get better. Hospitality. Sweat the experience. Delight customers, candidates and colleagues, even when it’s inconvenient. Transparency. Public unless private. Share context openly within the company so people and agents can take initiative. End-to-end. Deliver outcomes, not tasks. Step beyond your job description and see the work through. The role We're building strategic finance from scratch, and you'd be our first hire in it. You'd be the finance partner to every function, Sales, Marketing, Engagement and Product, helping decide how we price, where we invest and how we scale. You'd also own the numbers the company runs on: the operating model, the plan, and board and investor reporting. This is a hands-on role reporting directly to the Head of Finance, with no team between you and the work, and no part of it you won't touch. And you'll work closely on fundraising and investor relations. We're looking for someone a few years into banking, consulting, PE or strategic finance who wants to own outcomes instead of advising on them. You'd build your own models, dashboards and workflows with AI at the core, not bolted on. And we want someone who'd rather build the process than inherit one. Key ownership areas Partner with Sales, Marketing, Engagement and Product on the decisions that drive growth: pricing and packaging, sales capacity and quota planning, unit economics and payback, and GTM efficiency. Own the operating model, annual plan and forecasts, and track how we perform against them. Own monthly board and investor reporting, from the numbers through to the narrative. Build the analytics and dashboards leadership uses to run the business. Support fundraising and investor relations: model, materials, data room and investor Q&A. What you bring 2–4 years in investment banking, consulting, private equity or strategic finance. You can build an operating model from a blank sheet, not just update one. You turn messy data into a clear point of view, and can explain it plainly to a founder or a board member. You take a problem and own it. You'd rather deliver the answer than hand off the deck. You find building the playbook appealing. You're excited to use AI to do analysis faster and better, not just to use the tools you're handed. Bonus: SQL or data tooling (e.g. Hex), or exposure to B2B SaaS metrics. What's in it for you An environment that fosters cohesion, collaboration, and performance with transparency at the heart of what we do and how we communicate. Supreme rate-of-learning as we re-orient how the world works with AI. High compensation, through cash and equity. Unlimited AI - Unlimited access to ChatGPT, Claude, Cursor, and any other AI tools you need to move faster. Build your own toolkit - We'll provide the latest hardware, software, and equipment you need to do your best work. Ramp card for success - a company card to invest in the things that help you succeed: Lunches and coffees with interesting people Community memberships Event attendance Professional development Home office upgrades Books and learning resources Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

jobs.title: Superintendent Pharmacist
jobs.description: At Montu, every prescription represents a patient waiting for treatment that can make a genuine difference to their quality of life. Our pharmacy is at the heart of everything we do, processing over 50,000 prescriptions each month, with continued month-on-month growth of approximately 10%. We are looking for an experienced Superintendent Pharmacist to take ownership of clinical governance, regulatory compliance and professional standards across our rapidly growing, digital-first pharmacy. This is a senior leadership opportunity for someone with extensive knowledge of GPhC standards, MHRA regulations and Controlled Drugs governance, who can provide clear regulatory direction and ensure the pharmacy continues to operate safely, compliantly and efficiently as the business grows. Working closely with the General Manager of Pharmacy, Medical Director and wider senior leadership team, this role will be instrumental in shaping pharmacy strategy, strengthening governance frameworks and ensuring regulatory readiness for future expansion. This is not a traditional Superintendent Pharmacist position. The scale, pace and complexity of the operation require someone who can balance rigorous professional standards with commercial awareness, operational efficiency and a genuine commitment to patient safety. What is the Job? The Superintendent Pharmacist will have overall responsibility for the clinical and regulatory governance of Montu Pharmacy, ensuring all pharmacy activities meet the required professional, legal and regulatory standards. This includes providing professional leadership to a pharmacy team of over 100 people, overseeing Controlled Drugs governance, maintaining regulatory compliance and ensuring that systems, processes and Standard Operating Procedures are robust, effective and scalable. The role requires a hands-on, knowledgeable and confident leader who can identify regulatory risks, provide clear guidance to operational teams and take ownership of regulatory inspections, audits and continuous improvement. Alongside day-to-day governance, there is an opportunity to influence the wider pharmacy strategy, evaluate new services, support business expansion and contribute to the development of pharmacy technology and automation. What You Will Own Clinical Governance and Regulatory Compliance Take overall responsibility for clinical governance and professional standards across Montu Pharmacy. Ensure compliance with GPhC standards, MHRA regulations and all relevant statutory and professional requirements. Act as the senior regulatory expert within the pharmacy, providing clear guidance and direction to clinical and operational teams. Lead regulatory inspections, audits and compliance reviews, ensuring the pharmacy remains inspection-ready. Identify, assess and manage regulatory risks, implementing appropriate corrective and preventative actions. Ensure pharmacy policies, procedures and governance frameworks remain current, effective and fit for purpose. Maintain oversight of professional accountability, patient safety and regulatory reporting requirements. Controlled Drugs Governance Oversee Controlled Drugs governance, ensuring compliance with all relevant legislation and regulatory requirements. Ensure appropriate systems and controls are in place for the safe storage, handling, dispensing, recording and management of Controlled Drugs. Maintain accurate, auditable records and ensure appropriate monitoring and reconciliation processes are followed. Identify and address potential compliance risks, incidents or discrepancies. Support the development of scalable Controlled Drugs governance processes as prescription volumes increase. Professional Leadership and Team Development Provide professional and clinical leadership to a pharmacy workforce of over 100 people. jobs.description: Company Overview Deepgram is the leading platform underpinning the emerging trillion-dollar Voice AI economy, providing real-time APIs for speech-to-text (STT), text-to-speech (TTS), and building production-grade voice agents at scale. More than 200,000 developers and 1,300+ organizations build voice offerings that are ‘Powered by Deepgram’, including Twilio, Cloudflare, Sierra, Decagon, Vapi, Daily, Cresta, Granola, and Jack in the Box. The Opportunity Voice is the most natural modality for human interaction with machines. However, current sequence modeling paradigms based on jointly scaling model and data cannot deliver voice AI capable of universal human interaction. The challenges are rooted in fundamental data problems posed by audio: real-world audio data is scarce and enormously diverse, spanning a vast space of voices, speaking styles, and acoustic conditions. Even if billions of hours of audio were accessible, its inherent high dimensionality creates computational and storage costs that make training and deployment prohibitively expensive at world scale. We believe that entirely new paradigms for audio AI are needed to overcome these challenges and make voice interaction accessible to everyone. The Role As a Member of the Research Staff, you will pioneer the development of Latent Space Models (LSMs), a new approach that aims to solve the fundamental data, scale, and cost challenges associated with building robust, contextualized voice AI. Your research will focus on solving one or more of the following problems: Build next-generation neural audio codecs that achieve extreme, low bit-rate compression and high fidelity reconstruction across a world-scale corpus of general audio. Pioneer steerable generative models that can synthesize the full diversity of human speech from the codec latent representation, from casual conversation to highly emotional expression to complex multi-speaker scenarios with environmental noise and overlapping speech. Develop embedding systems that cleanly factorize the codec latent space into interpretable dimensions of speaker, content, style, environment, and channel effects -- enabling precise control over each aspect and the ability to massively amplify an existing seed dataset through “latent recombination”. Leverage latent recombination to generate synthetic audio data at previously impossible scales, unlocking joint model and data scaling paradigms for audio. Endeavor to train multimodal speech-to-speech systems that can 1) understand any human irrespective of their demographics, state, or environment

jobs.title: BizOps Manager
jobs.description: About Foundation Health Foundation Health is an AI operating system for pharmacy - built by a team who lived the problem firsthand, not one that came to healthcare from the outside. Every day, prior authorizations delay prescriptions, pharmacists lose hours to paperwork instead of patients, and prescriptions slip through the cracks between health systems. We believe thoughtfully applied AI can finally change that - deep, integrated infrastructure that streamlines how care is coordinated, purpose-built for the complexity of specialty pharmacy. We're building toward a world where pharmacy teams spend their time on patients, not paperwork - where AI handles the routine so clinicians can focus on what only humans can do. Getting there takes the right people. We're looking for curious, ambitious folks who want to help solve healthcare's hardest problems - for our patients, our partners, and each other. The Role Foundation Health is building AI-native pharmacy infrastructure, used by health systems, consumer health brands and pharma manufacturers. We're ~70 people, Series A, and growing quickly across the UK and US — and the operational engine behind the product needs to grow just as fast. That's where you come in. You'll be the right hand to our BizOps Director, working closely with our COO and with genuine visibility across senior leadership — the work you do here gets seen, used, and built on. You'll pick up the projects that don't fit neatly into any one team and run them from problem framing through to done, and you'll help shape the roadmap for what we take on next, not just deliver what's already on it. This is a generalist role in the truest sense. We're not looking for someone who's done one thing deeply — we're looking for someone who's done lots of things well, and can pick up whatever comes next. You'll also be working with AI at a depth most companies can't offer: it's the core of what we build and how we work, not something bolted on. And as we scale, this role scales with you — the scope is genuinely yours to grow. What You'll Be Doing No two weeks here look the same. Day to day could involve any of the below — and that variety is a big part of what makes the role interesting: Strategic projects — taking a loosely-framed problem, structuring it, doing the analysis, and driving it to implementation — while feeding into the roadmap for where we go next. Procurement & vendor management — sourcing, negotiating with, and managing the tools and vendors that keep the company running — from helpdesk platforms to AI tooling. Contracts & legal — supporting responses to RFIs, RFPs and bids from major US health systems, reviewing agreements, and getting comfortable in the commercial detail. Pricing — understanding what our solutions cost to deliver and modelling what we should sell them at. We’ve built a tiered, usage-based pricing structure from the cost-of-goods up — you’ll help evolve it as the product grows. Commercial & partnerships — supporting sales, client onboarding, and building the collateral and internal tools that help the commercial team move faster. Cross-functional work — partnering with sales, engineering, CX, product, and design to get things over the line. InfoSec & compliance — we operate in a HIPAA-regulated environment with a SOC 2 posture and an active certification programme. You’ll help run controls, policies and third-party risk assessments. You don’t need to be a security specialist, but you should bring a methodology and framework mindset. Who We're Looking For 3+ years in a technology, AI, data, or engineering-focused consulting environment. High-performing senior consultants ready to step up, and managers who want more scope than a big firm will give them, are exactly the sweet spot. A genuinely broad project history. jobs.title: Product and Technical Communications
jobs.description: TL;DR - Lovable ships fast. When millions of people build real businesses on your platform, both the product story and the trust story have to be airtight. You’ll own product and technical communications that makes sure this is the case: launches, trust and incident response, and the narrative that connects what we build to why it matters. Why Lovable? Lovable is the software creation platform that gives people the power to act on the problems closest to them. For decades, turning an idea into software required so much capital, technical fluency, and time that many ideas never came to life. Lovable is the counterargument: a platform for all people with ideas, ambition, and problems worth solving. From solopreneurs to small business owners to teams at companies like Adidas and Zendesk, people have built over 60 million projects on Lovable since its launch in November 2024. And we’re just getting started. We’re building a generational company from Stockholm, with growing teams in London, Boston, New York, and San Francisco. Our team is small, talent-dense, and moving quickly, with a culture rooted in extreme ownership, high velocity, and low-ego collaboration. We look for people who care deeply, ship fast, and are eager to make a dent in the world. Lovable is one of TIME’s 100 Most Influential Companies and has been recognized on the Forbes AI 50 and CNBC Disruptor 50, reflecting our momentum as one of Europe’s fastest-growing AI companies and one of the most ambitious places to build in this next era of software. What you’ll do Own trust, security, and incident communications. People build real businesses on Lovable, and their confidence in the platform is existential to ours. You’ll own Lovable’s trust narrative in earned and new media, proactively telling the story of how we think about security, privacy, reliability, and platform safety. And when something doesn’t go as planned, you’ll be the comms lead in the room, working alongside the Head of Communications to manage the external response with a cross-functional team. Lead product launch communications. When Lovable ships something new, you own the earned media strategy around it, including knowing the right Substacks, podcasts, and new media channels beyond traditional outlets. You’ll work closely with product marketing to shape positioning, develop press materials, pitch the story, and make sure launches land. The role sits at the interface between synthetic chemistry, cheminformatics and software, and lab automation, and you will build the computational capability alongside the physical synthesis and automation capability from an early stage. The role is embedded with the synthetic chemists and the automation scientists and engineers, and you will work with them every day. Much of the value comes from drawing out what experienced chemists know and turning their judgement into rules, models and workflows that apply the same way every time. Two parts of the role go beyond standard computational chemistry, and they are why it matters so much. Routes that automation can execute. A chemically plausible route is only the starting point. Planning has to account for what the platform can do, including the building blocks and reagents available, the reaction classes and conditions it supports, handling constraints, work-up and purification, and throughput. Given hundreds or thousands of targets, you will find the shared chemistry, common intermediates and building blocks, and reduce them to a manageable set of synthetic strategies, balancing diversity and compound value against synthetic cost.
